speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your sudden-onset lower back pain in detail: where is it located, does it travel down your leg, and what is the severity? Also, do you notice any numbness, weakness, or tingling in your leg or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Radiculopathy (likely L5 or S1 nerve root compression) secondary to acute muscle strain or disc herniation.

This diagnosis is based on your age, the sudden onset of sharp pain while exercising, and the specific radiation pattern down the side of your leg into the foot. To confirm the level of nerve involvement and rule out a large disc herniation, please describe any specific numbness or weakness you are feeling, and I will request an MRI of your lumbar spine for definitive imaging.
